text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said it still expected a good result for 1996, despite high credit risk provisions.

Chief executive officer Mathis Cabiallavetta, in a statement presented at UBS's traditional annual gathering for media in French-speaking western Switzerland, said the final outcome would still be determined by the state of financial markets in the second half of the year.
"The evolution of financial markets will determine the final outcome, but it is clear that we are not just sitting on our hands," Cabiallavetta said in a speech prepared for delivery here.
UBS will strive to reinforce its position abroad in an efficient manner, Cabiallavetta added.
He also confirmed that UBS wanted to be amongst the leading banks in the world and he was convinced the bank would achieve this.
On August 5, UBS said it expected good results for 1996, even though it did not assume the second half would be as successful as the first half.
For the first six months UBS reported a group net profit of 1.1 billion Swiss francs ($912.6 million) , up 33 percent from the same period in 1995. ($ = 1.205 Swiss Francs)
